notes: §1989:A.2.38.3 AR1: "Argument-1 must be class alphabetic or alphanumeric and must be at least one character in length." CheckArgumentClasses screens the Verified REVERSE row at every edition: Violation admits class alphabetic, alphanumeric or national (a class-worded row, so the edited categories and a group pass, as 1985's class alphanumeric requires) and PredicateViolation's minimum-width arm refuses a zero-length argument; the class national that §2023:15.78.3 adds cannot reach the screen at 85, where national items and literals are refused by UsageConstructId and VisitNonNumericLiteral (COBOL0900). Probed at 85: alphanumeric, alphabetic, numeric edited, alphanumeric edited and group items, a literal, a reference modification, a table element and a nested alphanumeric function are accepted and reversed; a numeric item, a COMP item, a numeric literal, an arithmetic expression and an integer function are refused with COBOL1627, and a zero-length literal with COBOL1627 and COBOL0900. The witness is the numeric-item refusal.

next.reason: 1985: "Argument-1 must be class alphabetic or alphanumeric"; 2023: "Argument-1 shall be of class alphabetic, alphanumeric, or national". Same REVERSE argument rule and the same minimum length of one, but 2023 also accepts class national arguments: a case is added.
